# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users to New Billing System

**Approach:** Both systems run in parallel (dual-write/dual-read where applicable) throughout the migration. Users are cut over in increasing batches; the old system remains fully operational as a fallback until well after 100% of users are migrated and stable.

---

## Phase 1 — Pilot (Canary)
- **Users:** 1% (400 of 40,000), internal accounts and opted-in low-risk customers
- **Entry criterion:** New system passes 100% of UAT test cases; a 2-week dual-write reconciliation dry run (no live customer cutover) shows matching ledgers on 100% of sampled transactions; rollback procedure has been executed successfully in staging.

## Phase 2 — Early Adopters
- **Users:** 9% (3,600 of 40,000) — cumulative 10% (4,000 users)
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 1 has run at least 14 consecutive days with zero Sev1/Sev2 incidents; billing discrepancy rate under 0.1%; billing-related support ticket volume no more than 10% above pre-migration baseline.

## Phase 3 — Broad Rollout
- **Users:** 40% (16,000 of 40,000) — cumulative 50% (20,000 users)
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 2 has run at least 14 consecutive days; payment success rate ≥99.5%; reconciliation mismatch rate under 0.05% of transaction value; support ticket volume within 15% of baseline; new system has been load-tested at 150% of projected peak volume.

## Phase 4 — General Availability (Final Migration Batch)
- **Users:** 50% (20,000 of 40,000) — cumulative 100% (40,000 users)
- **Entry criterion:** Phase 3 has run at least 21 consecutive days at scale with payment success rate sustained ≥99.5%; no open Sev1 incidents; finance has signed off on reconciliation accuracy for 3 consecutive billing cycles; traffic ramp-up staged over 72 hours rather than an instant cutover.

## Phase 5 — Legacy System Decommission (Separate from Final Migration Batch)
- **Users:** 0% (no user migration occurs in this phase — the old system is kept fully running through Phase 4 and beyond)
- **Entry criterion:** All 40,000 users have been on the new system for at least 60 days (minimum 2 full billing cycles) with zero critical billing discrepancies during that window; historical data has been archived from the old system and validated against the new system; legal, finance, and audit have all signed off before any decommissioning, disabling, or deletion of the old billing system begins.

---

## Risks

RISK: Dual-write reconciliation drift causes customers to be double-charged or under-charged during the overlap period | Run automated nightly reconciliation comparing old and new ledgers; auto-flag any variance greater than $1.00 or 0.1% of transaction value for manual review before the next batch proceeds | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Data migration errors corrupt customer billing records (wrong payment method, subscription tier, or proration) | Validate every migrated account against a checksum of source records, migrate in reversible batches, and manually spot-check a random 2% sample per batch before sign-off | Data Migration Team Lead
RISK: New system cannot handle production-scale transaction volume during the final batch, causing payment delays or failures | Load-test at 150% of projected peak volume before Phase 3; ramp Phase 4 traffic over 72 hours instead of an instant cutover | Platform SRE Lead
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing-related inquiries during migration, delaying resolution and harming trust | Train support staff two weeks ahead of Phase 2, stand up a dedicated migration escalation queue, and add on-call coverage for the first 72 hours of each phase | Customer Support Manager

---

## Halt Criteria

The rollout is halted immediately, no further batches proceed, and remaining users stay on the old system if either of the following is observed:
- Payment failure rate for migrated users exceeds **1.0%** sustained over any rolling 4-hour window (baseline failure rate on the old system is approximately 0.2%).
- Reconciliation mismatch between old and new ledgers exceeds **0.5% of daily transaction value** in any single day.

Resumption requires root-cause analysis and remediation, followed by re-verification of the entry criterion for the phase in progress.

---

**Arithmetic check:** 400 + 3,600 + 16,000 + 20,000 = 40,000 (100%); cumulative checkpoints of 1%, 10%, 50%, 100% are consistent with the stated per-phase percentages.

PHASES: 5
